one_month_reasoning: No NVDA print in the window: Q3 FY27 is expected ~Nov 17 (unconfirmed; some calendars say Nov 25), after 2026-11-04. In-window industry events: TSMC Q3 results/Q4 guide and ASML orders (mid-Oct; TSMC monthly sales +53% and CoWoS fully booked argue for a solid print); SK Hynix/Samsung Q3 (late Oct; HBM 2027 pricing, a demand signal but also NVDA's memory-cost squeeze); MSFT/GOOGL/META/AMZN Q3 (Oct 27-30; first explicit 2027 capex guides against a Big-4 consensus of ~$935B, +28% on 2026's ~$732B, so the bar is a re-acceleration claim that has to be confirmed); AMD Q3 (~early Nov; MI450/Helios). Macro: FOMC Oct 28 (~17% hike priced per the supervisor's check) and the Nov 3 midterms, both two-sided. Net: news skew modestly positive for demand but these are second-hand reads, and the stock sits at its 52-week high. I stay symmetric around spot at monthly vol ~11.2% (38%/3.5 plus a little for FOMC/midterms), median at spot; unchanged in substance from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (Oct-2027 NTM EPS, Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29, $16.9 x 16x = $270, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (NTM NI $404B x 72% conversion = ~$12.2 FCF/share at a 5.0% yield = $243 plus ~$2/share net cash = $245, weight 0.4), giving ~$260 (+10%). Down from $287: FCF conversion cut from 90% to 72% after the supervisor's filing check, FY29 growth cut from +18% to +13% because Big-4 2027 capex consensus is only +28%, and the horizon multiple lowered from 17x to 16x.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 NTM EPS (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29, same window as today's 19.3-19.5x) $16.9 x 16x

inputs_detail.derivation: Management's preliminary FY28 ~+70% (verified verbatim in the call transcript by the supervisor); consensus $687.45B on FY27 $411.6B.

Big-4 2027 capex consensus $934.5B vs 2026 guidance $732.5B = +28% (IO Fund); TrendForce sees NVL72 rack shipments +50% and rack value $710B in 2027 but ASIC growth (44.6% vs GPU 16.1% in 2026 per TrendForce snippet) and Meta accelerating its own ASICs in 2027. Growth into CY2028 (NVDA FY29) should slow toward the low-teens as capex growth decelerates (bank forecasts ~+10-15% for 2028); I use +13% EPS, down from +18% in round 1.

H2 FY28 = 15.80 - (3.17+3.63) = $9.00; H1 FY29 ~47% x 17.85 = $8.39; sum $17.39, less ~3% for memory-cost pressure (GM 71-72% Q4 trough, 72-73% FY28; $279B mostly-memory supply commitments) = $16.9. Consistent window with today's NTM basis, as the supervisor confirmed.

Today ~19.3-19.5x NTM (stockanalysis 19.34x; Fool $12.00 NTM). At-scale anchor AVGO 20.49x / TSM 20.65x (median 20.57x); the 11-peer median 36.7x is not used because it is inflated by early-ramp earnings (AMD, MRVL, ARM). At the horizon NVDA's NTM growth falls to low-teens (vs AVGO/TSM 3Y EPS CAGR forecasts of 40-65%), so I apply ~22% below the anchor. I do not stack a separate concentration discount on top (AVGO sells to the same hyperscalers, per supervisor). 16x is inside the peer range. The supervisor's break-even is ~13.5x, so this assumes ~3.5 turns of compression but not an EPS break.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM NI $16.9 x 23.9B shares = $404B; 72% conversion = $291B FCF = $12.2/share; 5.0% yield = $243; + ~$2/share net cash

inputs_detail.derivation: $16.9 NTM EPS (P/E leg) x 23.9B diluted shares.

Supply commitments rose to $279B, mostly memory, with ~$267B due by end FY29, so prepayments and inventory keep absorbing cash through the horizon; I use 72%, the H1 rate, not the weak Q2 nor round-1's unsupported 90%.
24.285B diluted in Q2 FY27 less buybacks (~$26B/qtr returned to shareholders).
~20x FCF, close to the AVGO/TSM ~20.6x P/E anchor; not lower because the 10Y is ~5.26% (supervisor-verified Treasury data) and FCF growth decelerates into FY29.

True net cash $23.2-23.6B today (cash + marketable debt securities - debt; excludes equity stakes per supervisor) plus FCF in excess of ~$104B/yr buybacks and dividends and ~$25B equity investment commitments.

bear.story: 2027 capex digestion: Big-4 capex growth already slows to ~+28% in 2027 on consensus and hyperscalers are debt-funding capex (FactSet); 2028 orders slow, Meta/Google/AWS ASICs take share (TrendForce), AMD Helios wins; GM stuck ~71% as HBM costs on $279B of commitments bite. NTM EPS ~$13.5 x 12x (peak-cycle multiple) = ~$162-165.

base.story: FY28 delivers ~70% growth as guided (TrendForce NVL72 value +214% in 2027), price hikes partly offset HBM costs, but FY29 growth decelerates to low-teens and the multiple compresses to ~15.5-16x. NTM EPS ~$16.9 x ~15.7x = ~$265: earnings growth outruns compression.

bull.story: 2027 capex beats the $935B Big-4 consensus toward the $1.3-1.45T bank/TrendForce views, CoWoS demand +93% and HBM sold out translate into FY29 growth of 25%+ and margins back to mid-70s; NTM EPS ~$19.5 x 19x (back near the AVGO/TSM anchor) = ~$370.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact checks changed three things for me. (1) FCF conversion: the CFO commentary (re-read via sec.gov) shows Q2 FY27 FCF $21.3B vs non-GAAP NI $54.0B (39%) and H1 FCF $69.9B (~70%), DSO 60; my 90% was unsupported, so I use 72%, and the industry lane explains why it stays low: supply commitments jumped to $279B, mostly memory, ~$267B due by FY29 (TrendForce/Fool), so prepayments and inventory keep absorbing cash. FCF leg falls from $284 to $245. (2) Peer anchor: I now say plainly that I anchor on AVGO/TSM (20.57x), not the 36.7x median (which lacked AMAT), and I drop the separate concentration discount the supervisor said should not be stacked. (3) New lane evidence: IO Fund puts Big-4 2027 capex consensus at $934.5B vs $732.5B guided for 2026 (+28%), well below the '$1.3T' six-hyperscaler figure I leaned on in round 1 (TrendForce has ~$1.3T for the top nine CSPs, a wider set, seen only in a search snippet). TrendForce (Aug 28) still sees NVL72 rack value $710B in 2027 (+214%), so FY28 ~+70% looks safe, but growth into FY29 should decelerate harder, and ASICs are growing faster than GPUs. I cut FY29 EPS growth to +13% and the horizon multiple to 16x (~22% below the anchor, justified by the growth gap). Horizon NTM EPS (consistent Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 window) $16.9 x 16x = $270; FCF $245; blend $260 (+10%), slightly below the supervisor's $274 because of my lower FY29 growth. Scenarios: bear $165/25% (EPS $13.5 x 12x), base $265/50%, bull $370/25%, each with ~19-24% log dispersion. The mixture gives median ~$263 and P(>= spot) 0.62; tails fattened slightly beyond the lognormal mixture. Compression remains a drag on upside, not the main risk: the supervisor's break-even is ~13.5x, so losses need an EPS break, which is my bear case. 1-month ladder is symmetric at ~11% monthly vol because no NVDA print falls in the window. Limits: TrendForce ASIC-share and nine-CSP capex figures are search snippets (not used as sole support for any number); Bloomberg/CNBC were snippets in round 1. Context only: 61-analyst mean target $327.70.
